terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo runs your functions against the fake services and prints how long each one took.

tasks.title: Rewrite the report with await
tasks.description:
`sailingReport(route, services)` in `src/sailingReport.js` already works with `.then()`. Rewrite it as an `async` function that uses `await` and has no `.then(` left in it.

It must behave exactly as before:

- resolve with `{ route, time, sea }`
- call `getSailing(route)`, then `getSeaState(time)` with the sailing's time
- reject with the same error when either service fails, and skip `getSeaState` when `getSailing` fails

**Timing:** `services` is a parameter that defaults to the fake services. The check passes its own pair that answer on the next turn of the event loop.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.js` and note the two report lines.
Add `async` in front of the function.
Replace each `.then()` with a `const` and an `await`.
Run the demo again: the lines should not change.
hints: `await` pauses the async function until the promise settles and gives you its value. A rejection becomes a thrown error.
You do not need a try and catch here. An error thrown inside an async function rejects the promise it returns.
Two awaits, one after the other, then return an object that spreads the sailing and adds `sea`.

tasks.title: A dashboard that waits only when it must
tasks.description:
`loadDashboard(route, services)` in `src/dashboard.js` works, but it awaits three slow calls one after the other. Make it faster without changing what it returns: `{ sailings, weather, crew }`.

- start `getSailings(route)` and `getWeather(route)` before waiting for either
- call `getCrew(id)` with the first sailing's id as soon as the sailings arrive, without waiting for the weather
- with no sailings, `crew` is `[]` and `getCrew` is not called
- if `getWeather` rejects while the sailings are still loading, the dashboard rejects with that error and the rejection is never left unhandled

**Timing:** `services` is a parameter that defaults to the fake services. The check passes fakes it settles one at a time, and records which calls had started after each one.
nextSteps: Run the demo and note how long the dashboard takes.
Find which calls depend on which.
Start the independent work first and wait for it together.
Run the demo again: it should take about 700 ms instead of 1100.
hints: Calling an async function starts it. Awaiting it is a separate step you can do later.

Holding a started promise in a variable and awaiting it later is fast, but if it rejects before you reach the await, nobody is listening yet. `Promise.all` listens to every promise from the moment you give it to it.
Put 'sailings, then crew' in a small async function of its own, then wait for it and the weather with one `Promise.all`.

tasks.title: Save a booking and always unlock the seat
tasks.description:
Implement `saveBooking(booking, services)` in `src/booking.js`. A booking is `{ id, name, email, seat }`. It resolves with `{ saved: true, emailed }`.

- await `services.storeBooking(booking)`. If it rejects, reject with that same error and do not call `emailTicket`
- then await `services.emailTicket(booking)`. If it rejects, the booking still counts: resolve with `emailed: false`. Otherwise `emailed: true`
- call `services.unlockSeat(booking.seat)` exactly once in every case, after the other calls have settled
- no rejection may be left unhandled

**Timing:** `services` is a parameter that defaults to the fake services. The check passes fakes that answer on the next turn of the event loop and records the order of every call.
nextSteps: Write the happy path: store, email, return.
Wrap the email in its own try and catch.
Unlock the seat in a block that always runs.
Run the demo and read all three booking lines.
hints: Two different failures need two different answers: one is passed on to the caller, the other is turned into `emailed: false`.
`finally` runs after `try` finishes, whether it returned or threw, and it does not swallow the error.
A `try` only covers promises you `await` inside it. Calling `emailTicket` without `await` lets it fail later, outside your catch, and unlocks the seat too early.
